response.initial_request: The tenant reports that a Samsung television in an upstairs bedroom has an electrical fault and trips a fuse when plugged in; it is currently unplugged. They also report a downstairs bedroom light that flickers and makes a popping sound when switched on. Please arrange any property access in advance because a dog is at the property.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Reported that a Samsung TV in the upstairs bedroom had an internal electrical fault and, in the tenant's description, shorted out and repeatedly tripped a fuse when plugged in. The tenant said the TV had seen little overall use and was unplugged to avoid further damage. Also reported that the downstairs bedroom light flickered and made a popping noise when switched on. Asked that access be scheduled in advance because a dog was at the property.

Requested approval to arrange works for the TV fault, classifying the request as appliance repairs. The description included the tenant-reported shorting and repeated fuse trips, that the TV was unplugged, and the low reported use. This approval request did not include the downstairs light.

Replied, “Please sort it. I don't remember leaving a TV.” The reply followed the TV-focused request. It did not mention the downstairs light or expressly address ownership, replacement, or disposal of the television.

Recorded the landlord's instruction to proceed in response to the TV request, along with the landlord's uncertainty about whether the TV had been left at the property. No spending limit or specific disposal instruction was recorded.

Updated the maintenance record to include the downstairs bedroom light's flickering and popping symptoms. The tenant had included those symptoms in the initial report, but the landlord's approval request had concerned only the TV.
Requested availability for an electrical contractor to attend regarding the recorded TV and light issues. Asked the tenant to provide times in advance so access could be coordinated around the dog.
An automatic reply said the landlord was away. It contained no further repair instructions.
Followed up for appointment availability for the electrical visit and invited the tenant to share relevant access details.
Sent a brief reminder to check the email and provide availability for the maintenance visit.
No tenant availability had been received following the email and SMS. The electrical visit remained unscheduled.
Recorded a change of electrical contractor. The previous contractor was stood down and scheduling was restarted with Bracken Spark Services.
Requested appointment slots again for the combined electrical visit and noted that access needed to be arranged in advance.
Followed up for availability for the electrical visit.
Sent a brief reminder to reply with possible appointment times.

events.from: Jory Senn (Cover Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: Tenant said their partner had made the original report and they would send availability. The tenant said they had tried replacing fuses and believed the TV's main board was fried; this was the tenant's view, not a technician's diagnosis. They said the TV might as well be discarded if repair was not straightforward and were open to removal. The tenant said they were using a lamp instead of the downstairs light and could manage without it for now. They also raised a separate issue: the rear-door handle had come off. Jory could not find a record of that issue and asked the tenant to submit it separately; the tenant agreed.

Provided availability for an electrical visit: 23 September after 15:00, 24 September after 15:00, 25 September after 12:30, 29 September after 15:00, 30 September after 15:00, or 2 October after 12:30. Said the dog would be taken out during the visit and asked the contractor to call on arrival rather than knock.

Sent the electrician the reported TV fault and downstairs light symptoms together, with the tenant's available dates and request to call on arrival rather than knock because of the dog. Asked the electrician to propose a suitable visit slot. This was a combined electrical visit request; no separate appliance assessment or repair assignment, or decision about TV disposal, was recorded.
Noted that the rear-door handle had been raised during the call only. No separate report had been received, and no handyman had been assigned.
Proposed attending on 29 September after 15:00. No exact arrival time was offered, and no appointment confirmation had been sent.

args.subject: 8 Vellum Court, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ: approval needed for electrical visit (TV and bedroom light)
args.body:
Dear Mr Wex,

Re: 8 Vellum Court, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ. Thank you for your reply of 5 September asking us to sort the TV fault. We need two quick decisions before we confirm an electrician.

1. Downstairs bedroom light: the tenant reports it flickers and makes a popping noise when switched on. Your approval covered the TV only. May we include an inspection of this light, with the electrician resolving it where possible or quoting if significant, in the same visit? The tenant is using a lamp for now.

2. The TV: you said you do not remember leaving a TV. Do you know whether it belongs to the property? The tenant thinks the TV's main board has failed and is open to its removal. If it is the tenant's, the electrician's time on the TV would not be a landlord cost. Please tell us whether you want us to (a) have the electrician assess the TV, or (b) leave the TV out of the visit and cover only the light. Please also say whether you want any spending limit applied.

Bracken Spark Services has offered 29 September after 15:00, which is within the tenant's availability. We will confirm it once we hear from you.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

args.subject: Electrical visit update - 8 Vellum Court, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body:
Dear Ms Pell,

Thank you for your availability. The electrician has offered 29 September after 15:00, which matches one of your slots. We are waiting on the landlord to confirm the scope, including the downstairs light and the TV, before we confirm the visit. We will then confirm a time and ask the electrician to call on arrival because of the dog. Please keep the TV unplugged. Please also submit the rear-door handle as a separate request, as agreed on the call.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

args.reason: Waiting for Landlord: approval for the downstairs light, TV ownership and scope, needed before confirming Bracken Spark's 29 Sept visit. The landlord's auto-reply said they were away.

args.summary: Asked the landlord to approve the light inspection and to confirm TV ownership and scope. The visit is not confirmed yet. The tenant has been updated and a follow-up is set for 22 Sept.
facts: Landlord approval (event 3) was in reply to a TV-only request (event 2); no spending limit was recorded (event 4).
The downstairs light was never put to the landlord (events 2, 5).
The landlord said they do not remember leaving a TV (event 3). The tenant thinks the board is fried and is open to removing the TV (event 15).
The landlord's auto-reply says they are away (event 7).
The tenant offered slots (event 16). Bracken Spark proposed 29 Sept after 15:00, with no exact time and no confirmation sent (event 19).
The rear-door handle is a separate matter and has not been reported (events 15, 18).
conflicts: The landlord's approval covers only the TV, but the visit request combines the TV and the light (events 3, 17).
TV ownership and liability are unresolved (event 3).
missing: Landlord approval for the light work
Whether the TV is the landlord's, and whether to assess it
An exact arrival time from the electrician
options_rejected: Confirming the 29 Sept visit now: the light work has no landlord approval and the TV scope is uncertain.
Escalating: one landlord message can settle both questions.
Charging the tenant: there is no evidence of tenant damage or of who owns the TV.
args.uncertainty: The landlord is away, so a reply may be slow. If there is no reply by the follow-up date, chase again and consider escalating if the silence continues.
